definitions.explanation: The act of reading text out loud, such as reading names from a list, reciting results, or reading a document aloud to an audience.
A technology function in which a device or application converts written text into spoken audio. Common in accessibility features and language learning tools.

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}の{読|よ}み{上|あ}げが{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The reading aloud of names began.

examples.japanese: {司会者|しかいしゃ}が{結果|けっか}を{読|よ}み{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: The emcee read the results aloud.

examples.japanese: {卒業式|そつぎょうしき}で{校長|こうちょう}{先生|せんせい}が{卒業生|そつぎょうせい}の{名前|なまえ}を{一人|ひとり}ずつ{読|よ}み{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: At the graduation ceremony, the principal read out each graduate's name one by one.

examples.japanese: {読|よ}み{上|あ}げ{機能|きのう}をオンにする。
examples.english: I'll turn on the text-to-speech function.

examples.japanese: このアプリは{記事|きじ}を{音声|おんせい}で{読|よ}み{上|あ}げてくれる。
examples.english: This app reads articles aloud in audio.

examples.japanese: {視覚障害者|しかくしょうがいしゃ}のために、{画面|がめん}の{内容|ないよう}を{読|よ}み{上|あ}げるソフトが{開発|かいはつ}された。
examples.english: Software that reads screen content aloud was developed for visually impaired people.

notes:
USAGE:
The noun form of the verb {読|よ}み{上|あ}げる (to read aloud). Used both as a noun ({読|よ}み{上|あ}げ) and in verb form. In technology contexts, {読|よ}み{上|あ}げ{機能|きのう} (text-to-speech function) is extremely common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {読|よ}み{上|あ}げ{機能|きのう} (text-to-speech function)
- {読|よ}み{上|あ}げソフト (text-to-speech software)
- {音声|おんせい}{読|よ}み{上|あ}げ (audio reading)
- {名前|なまえ}を{読|よ}み{上|あ}げる (to read names aloud)
